title: Length-normalized priority scheduler with dynamic pad-budget trimming
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: reduce wasted padding and overall tail latency for mixed-length request distributions by normalizing scheduling priority to sequence length and introducing a budget-trimming pass that dynamically lowers padding allowance when kernel-fit cost exceeds benefit. This PR implements a length-normalized priority scheduler that scores slots by (priority / sqrt(request_length)) and a pad-budget trimming allocator that shrinks allowed slot padding based on recent kernel-fit histograms. Key outcomes: lower average tokens padded per batch, improved short-tail latency under mixed workloads, and preserved KV prefill behavior. Includes unit + integration tests and perf benchmarks. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (docs/notes/length-priority.md) [x] unit tests (tests/scheduler/length_priority_test.cpp) [x] perf harness run (perf/results/len-priority-20260224.csv) [x] add metrics (batch.pad_savings, scheduler.len_norm_score) [ ] canary rollout config (follow-up). Related: ENG-4021 for batching SLA improvement and ENG-4200 kernel-fit cost model integration.
